questions.prompt: What two types of nuclear processes does Keating say the lecture will discuss as producing energy in stars?
choices: A Only chemical combustion of wood.
B Nuclear processes that can yield self-sustaining reactions unlike ordinary chemistry.
C Purely magnetic storms with no nuclei.
D Only radioactive decay in Earth rocks.
questions.explain: He introduces nuclear processes that can be self-sustaining versus chemical reactions.

questions.prompt: What force does Keating emphasize as "smushing" protons together to enable solar fusion—without pumps or reactors?
choices: A Electromagnetism alone.
B Purely gravity.
C Human-built nuclear reactors inside the Sun.
D Planetary magnetism.
questions.explain: He stresses gravity alone compresses material enough for fusion.

questions.prompt: Galileo used sunspots, Keating notes, to measure roughly what solar rotation period?
choices: A 1 Earth day.
B About 28 Earth days.
C 365 days.
D One hour.
questions.explain: Keating says Galileo measured a ~28-Earth-day solar "day" via sunspots.

questions.prompt: Why does Keating say fusing iron marks the end of a massive star's life support against collapse?
choices: A Iron fusion releases the most energy of any fuel.
B Fusing iron takes more energy than it yields, so heat no longer holds gravity at bay.
C Iron turns into helium forever.
D Iron fusion only happens on Earth.
questions.explain: Iron fusion is endothermic in net stellar terms; collapse follows.

questions.prompt: Keating contrasts the original Earth-centered cosmology of Ptolemy and Aristotle with later models; what odd planetary behavior helped motivate epicycles?
choices: A Retrograde motion of planets like Mercury, Venus, and Mars.
B Stars never moving.
C Only lunar eclipses.
D Constant brightness of the Sun.
questions.explain: Retrograde motion forced complex Earth-centered constructions.
